subject: Evidence pruning playbook and TTL for vendor portal profiles
body:
From: security@brightleaf.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightleaf: evidence refresh cadence & vendor-portal pruning question

Hi Tessa,

Quick question from our procurement/security team as we finish the CAIQ submission: in Vendr and Whistic we see many legacy artifacts (old SOC2 bridge letters, rotated keys screenshots, expired cert bundles). Does Redwood have a recommended retention or pruning cadence for third-party portal evidence so we don’t overwhelm the profile reviewers?

Specifically:
- Do you prefer a snapshot-and-archive model (export current evidence to S3 and then remove from the portal)?
- Any TTL/tagging conventions you recommend so the portal only surfaces active evidence to your reviewers?
- Are there objections to automated expiration of attachments older than X months, with a link back to an archive?

We expect to start a monthly sync next week and wanted to align on approach before we push a bulk export.

Thanks,
Jane Doe
Security Program Manager
Brightleaf Health

---
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: security@brightleaf.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf: evidence refresh cadence & vendor-portal pruning question

Hi Jane — great timing. We’ve been iterating a lightweight evidence-pruning playbook for vendor profiles aimed at keeping portal inventories lean while preserving auditability. High-level proposal below; attaching the manifest template and draft playbook.

Proposal (summary):
- Snapshot & Archive: Export a monthly snapshot of profile evidence to a customer-dedicated S3 bucket (immutable folder per snapshot). Tag the snapshot with date and CAIQ/SIG/SOC2 mapping.
- Portal TTL Tags: In Vendr/Whistic add a TTL label for non-authoritative artifacts (screenshots, ad-hoc logs). Default TTL = 180 days; SOC2 reports and canonical attestations are "essential" and not auto-pruned.
- Soft-delete + Linkback: When evidence crosses TTL, soft-delete from portal and replace with a pointer that references the archived snapshot (preserves reviewer flow).
- Audit trail: Keep a CSV manifest (example attached) that lists removed items, reason, and S3 path. The manifest is versioned and surfaced to auditors.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Brightleaf: confirm which artifact classes are "essential" vs "ephemeral" (we can provide a short rubric).
2) We'll provision an S3 snapshot prefix and a small lambda to publish manifests and pointer records.
3) 30-min sync: propose Thu 07/01 10:00 PT to walk the playbook and test a sample export.

Attachments: evidence-manifest-template.csv, evidence-pruning-playbook-v1.docx

Thanks — looping in Laura and Marcus for compliance scope + Priyom for infra ops.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Vendor Security Operations
Redwood Inference

---
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, security@brightleaf.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf: evidence refresh cadence & vendor-portal pruning question

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 10:05 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Jane — great timing. We’ve been iterating a lightweight evidence-pruning playbook for vendor profiles aimed at keeping portal inventories lean while preserving auditability.

Thanks — couple clarifications from compliance:
- SOC2/ISO artifacts: these should always be marked "preserve". If Brightleaf has a SOC2 bridge letter or table of scope, we want that retained in the portal and in the snapshot.
- CAIQ question/answers: we prefer the live Q&A to remain editable in the portal, but attachments supporting CAIQ answers (e.g., screenshots) can follow TTL rules.
- Retention length: 180 days TTL for ephemeral items sounds fine for first pass, but on the manifest please include a column for proposed retention override so customers can request 365d for evidence tied to active procurement windows.

Also please add a short note in the playbook about how to handle redlines/contract snapshots (these are often requested by legal audits).

--
Laura Bennett
Sr. Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

---
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: security@brightleaf.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf: evidence refresh cadence & vendor-portal pruning question

Thanks all — confirmed for the playbook approach and the sync. Action items:
- Brightleaf: within 48 hours, send a short list of artifacts to mark as "essential" (SOC2 docs, encryption attestations, contract redline snapshots).
- Redwood Ops (Priyom): provision the S3 snapshot prefix and share write-only creds in the sync.
- Compliance (Laura): add the "retention override" column to the manifest and a short blurb on contract snapshots.

I uploaded the draft playbook and a short s3-snapshot-playbook.md to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-playbook — please review before Thu 07/01 10:00 PT.

Attachments referenced (placeholders in thread):
- evidence-manifest-template.csv (CSV with columns: snapshot_id, artifact_name, portal_id, artifact_type, created_at, ttl_days, override_requested_by, s3_path)
- evidence-pruning-playbook-v1.docx (word doc: procedures + roles + sample manifest)
- s3-snapshot-playbook.md (internal ops checklist for snapshot lambda)

If Brightleaf prefers to keep everything in the portal instead of archive + pointer, we can run a pilot with a shorter TTL (90 days) and evaluate reviewer load metrics after 2 months.

See you Thu.

Regards,
Tessa
Head of Vendor Security Operations
Redwood Inference
